rules.statement: A testator's intention to settle property on their real descendants, as far as possible, can be inferred from a clause that prohibits alienation and provides for the property to escheat to the Crown only upon the extinction of all generations of descendants.
rules.supporting_quote: "It is difficult to believe that the language of the testators was used with no other intention than that of appointing the condition upon which the property was to escheat to the Crown regardless of the circumstance that during the lives of successive generations of their descendants the property may by alienation have passed into the hands of strangers."
